reason: Both conversations repeated the 'plug a kettle into the socket' test after being told it was a hardwired switch and neither suggested the simple, acceptable step of swapping the BS1362 fuse in the spur carrier. Conversation 1 was worse on safety and listening: it twice told a self-declared non-wiring-literate homeowner to remove the spur faceplate (where incoming terminals stay live even with the switch off) after they had explicitly declined, and it ignored the direct question 'could it be a fuse in the spur?'. Conversation 2 at least obtained the make/model, avoided pushing the user into the wiring, and escalated to an engineer, though it marked itself down by asserting without evidence that the 'mains input module or control board has failed'. On balance Conversation 2 served the homeowner slightly better, mainly on safety and respecting the user's stated limits.
